mainTopic: Footwear on יום הכפורים, children's exemptions, and leniencies for a king, a bride, and a new mother
overview: The גמרא finishes asking whether a cork sandal counts as a forbidden shoe on יום הכפורים. Eyewitnesses report that great sages wore cork, reed, or palm-fiber sandals, or even wrapped a scarf around their feet. רמי בר חמא objects from a ברייתא that forbids an amputee's wooden leg on יום הכפורים. אביי's answer, that the padding is the problem, is knocked down by רבא, who explains that everyone agrees the wooden leg is a real shoe. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue only about a שבת decree. Next, a ברייתא teaches that children may do everything on יום כיפור except wear shoes. The reason given is that bathing and anointing are needed for a child's growth, and shoes are not. The גמרא then explains the משנה's leniency for a king and a bride to wash their faces, which follows רבי אליעזר, and it defines a bride as a woman in her first thirty days of marriage. A new mother may wear shoes because of the cold, and שמואל permits shoes where there is danger from scorpions. Finally, the גמרא quotes the משנה's measure for eating, a large date's volume, and introduces a question from רב פפא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is a cork sandal allowed on יום הכפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The end of the question: may one go out in a cork sandal on יום הכפורים?
steps.simpleTranslation: [May one go out in a sandal of] cork on יום הכפורים?
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish a question that began on the previous page: may a person wear a cork sandal on יום הכפורים? This question sets up the testimonies that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a shoe is one of the forbidden afflictions of יום הכפורים. The question is whether footwear that is not made of leather, like cork, counts as a 'shoe' for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Cork, or a soft bark-like material

phrases.english: [a sandal of] cork on Yom Kippur?
phrases.notes: The question began on the previous page with 'what is the law about going out in a sandal of...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a cork sandal count as a forbidden shoe on יום הכפורים?

steps.title: Testimony that רבי יהושע בן לוי wore cork on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני testifies that he saw רבי יהושע בן לוי wear cork sandals on יום הכפורים, and was told that a תענית צבור is no different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני stood up and said: I saw רבי יהושע בן לוי go out in a cork sandal on יום הכפורים. I asked him: what about a public fast? He said: it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: An eyewitness answers the question: a great sage was seen wearing cork sandals on יום הכפורים. The witness also asked about a public fast and was told the same rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This testimony answers the question with an actual practice: cork is not a forbidden 'shoe.' The follow-up question shows the rule carries over to a תענית צבור, where shoes are also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood on his feet, a sign of formal testimony
A public fast declared for a crisis, such as a drought

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי עַל רַגְלָיו,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani stood on his feet,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: and said: I saw Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיָּצָא בְּסַנְדָּל שֶׁל שַׁעַם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: go out in a sandal of cork on Yom Kippur.
And I said to him: What about a public fast?
He said to me: It is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי עַל רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1 with an eyewitness report.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cork sandals are permitted on יום הכפורים, and also on a תענית צבור.

steps.title: Testimony that רבי אלעזר of Nineveh wore cork on a public fast
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה saw רבי אלעזר of Nineveh wear cork sandals on a תענית צבור and was told יום הכפורים is no different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: I saw רבי אלעזר from Nineveh go out in a cork sandal on a public fast. I asked him: what about יום הכפורים? He said: it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: A second eyewitness backs up the same ruling, this time starting from a public fast and asking about יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the first testimony. Together, the two reports show from both sides that cork sandals are allowed on both kinds of fast.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּמִן נִנְוֵה
phrases.english: I saw Rabbi Elazar from Nineveh

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיָּצָא בְּסַנְדָּל שֶׁל שַׁעַם בְּתַעֲנִית צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: go out in a sandal of cork on a public fast,
and I said to him: What about Yom Kippur?
He said to me: It is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel testimony supporting step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that cork sandals are permitted on fast days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי אלעזר of Nineveh, reported by רבה בר בר חנה

steps.title: How various אמוראים went out on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, אביי, and רבא wore sandals of reeds or palm fiber, and רבה בר רב הונא wrapped a scarf around his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה went out in reed sandals. אביי went out in palm-fiber sandals. רבא went out in braided-reed sandals. רבה בר רב הונא wrapped a scarf around his feet and went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists more real-life examples of sages wearing non-leather foot coverings on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these materials, such as reeds, palm fiber, and cloth, are treated as 'not a shoe.' The scarf example will matter later, because it shows that foot comfort by itself is not forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The practice of רבה בר רב הונא is used in step 8 to reject אביי's answer.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda went out in reed sandals.
Abaye went out in palm-fiber sandals.
Rava went out in braided-reed sandals.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא כָּרֵיךְ סוּדָרָא אַכַּרְעֵיהּ וְנָפֵיק.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna wrapped a scarf around his feet and went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more practical examples that support the leniency.
steps.raayaObject: Non-leather foot coverings are permitted on יום הכפורים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practices of רב יהודה, אביי, רבא, and רבה בר רב הונא

steps.title: Objection from the amputee's wooden leg
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא cites a ברייתא: all agree an amputee may not go out on his wooden leg on יום הכפורים, which suggests non-leather footwear is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: An amputee may go out with his wooden leg on שבת, says רבי מאיר, and רבי יוסי forbids it. A ברייתא adds: and they agree that it is forbidden to go out with it on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא challenges all the lenient practices. He points to a source where a wooden foot, which is not leather, is forbidden on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wooden prosthetic leg counts as a shoe and is forbidden on יום הכפורים, then cork, reed, and palm-fiber sandals should also be forbidden. The leniency of steps 2 through 4 seems to clash with this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An amputee, someone missing a leg
And a ברייתא was taught about it

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama raised an objection:
An amputee may go out with his wooden leg [on Shabbat],

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir. And Rabbi Yosei forbids it.
And it was taught about it:

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאָסוּר לָצֵאת בּוֹ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: And they agree that it is forbidden to go out with it on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leniency established by the testimonies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to wear non-leather footwear on יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wooden leg is not leather, yet everyone forbids it on יום הכפורים. So non-leather footwear should be forbidden too.

steps.title: אביי: the wooden leg is forbidden because of its padding
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the wooden leg has rag padding, and it is forbidden because of the comfort, not because it is a shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There, it has rags inside it, and it is forbidden because of the pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the lenient practices. He says the wooden leg is forbidden for a different reason: its soft padding gives comfort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the ברייתא is not about the shoe rule at all. It is about a padded leg that provides pleasure, so it says nothing against cork or reed sandals.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָתָם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ כְּתִיתִין,
phrases.english: Abaye said: There, it is where it has rags in it,
and it is forbidden because of pleasure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָתָם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ כְּתִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ברייתא is about a padded leg
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wooden leg is forbidden because it counts as a shoe.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden only because of the comfort from its padding.

steps.title: רבא: rags cannot turn it into a shoe
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if the wooden leg is not a shoe, adding rags does not make it one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If it is not a shoe, do rags make it into a shoe?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins attacking אביי's answer. This is the first of three arguments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden act on יום הכפורים is wearing a shoe. Padding does not change what the object is, so it cannot be the reason for forbidding it.

keyTerms.meaning: An item, here meaning a shoe

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And if it is not a shoe,
do rags make it into a shoe?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְאִי לָאו מָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's explanation that the padding causes the prohibition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Padding does not change the object's category. If it is not a shoe, it stays not a shoe.

steps.title: רבא: comfort alone is not forbidden on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second argument: comfort that does not come from a shoe is not forbidden, as shown by רבה בר רב הונא's scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: is every pleasure that is not a shoe forbidden on יום הכפורים? But רבה בר רב הונא used to wrap a scarf around his feet and go out!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second argument against אביי, using a practice we already saw in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים forbids specific afflictions, and wearing a shoe is one of them. General comfort is not forbidden. The scarf of רבה בר רב הונא proves that soft foot comfort is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: כׇּל תַּעֲנוּג דְּלָאו מִנְעָל הוּא,
phrases.english: And furthermore: any pleasure that is not a shoe,
is it forbidden on Yom Kippur?
But Rabba bar Rav Huna
would wrap a scarf around his feet and go out!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: כׇּל תַּעֲנוּג דְּלָאו מִנְעָל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second argument against אביי, drawing on step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's idea that comfort itself is forbidden
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only shoes are forbidden, not comfort in general, as רבה בר רב הונא's practice shows.

steps.title: רבא: the later clause shows the case has no padding
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third argument: the end of the ברייתא speaks separately about a leg with a padding compartment, so the first part must be about a leg without padding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, since the later clause teaches: if it has a compartment for rags, it can become טמא, this shows that the first clause is not dealing with one that has rags.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third argument against אביי, this time from the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending of the source introduces the padded case as something new. That means the opening case, which is the one forbidden on יום הכפורים, has no padding. So padding cannot be the reason it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a source
The first clause of a source

steps.whatToRemember: All three of רבא's arguments knock down אביי's padding explanation, so the challenge of רמי בר חמא needs a new answer.

phrases.english: And furthermore, since the later clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִבּוּל כְּתִיתִין — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: If it has a receptacle for rags, it is susceptible to impurity,
this implies that in the first clause
we are not dealing with one that has rags.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third and final argument against אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's reading of the case in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's own structure shows the first case has no padding.

steps.title: רבא: everyone agrees it is a shoe, and the argument is about a שבת decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that all agree the wooden leg counts as a shoe. רבי יוסי forbids it on שבת because of a decree that it might fall off and be carried four אמות, while רבי מאיר does not make that decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Really, everyone agrees it is a shoe. On שבת they argue about this: one holds we decree it is forbidden, in case it slips off and he comes to carry it four אמות, and the other holds we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting אביי, רבא gives his own explanation of the ברייתא. He sets up a new understanding of the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the wooden leg counts as a shoe for everyone, the ruling that it is forbidden on יום הכפורים is simple. The argument about שבת is not over whether it is a shoe. It is about whether חכמים made a protective decree against carrying in a public area.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a new approach after a rejection
We make a protective rabbinic decree
Four cubits, the distance that counts as forbidden carrying in a public domain

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי holds that the wooden leg is not a shoe. In רבא's view, everyone agrees it is a shoe. רבי יוסי only adds a decree because of carrying on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole argument from a question of what a 'shoe' is into a question about a שבת decree. It also closes the cork-sandal discussion: the wooden leg is forbidden on יום הכפורים because it is a real shoe, so it poses no challenge to the non-leather sandals of steps 2–4. The next step moves to a new topic, children on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Actually, according to everyone it is a shoe,
and regarding Shabbat, this is what they disagree about:
One Sage holds that we decree

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט וְאָתֵי לְאֵתוֹיֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: lest it slip off and he come to carry it four cubits,
and one Sage holds that we do not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִנְעָל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about whether a wooden leg counts as a shoe.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees it is a shoe, which is why it is forbidden on יום הכפורים. They argue only about a שבת decree against carrying.

steps.title: Children may do everything except wear shoes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that young children are permitted in all the יום כיפור restrictions, except wearing a sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: young children are allowed to do all of the restricted activities, except wearing a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about children on יום כיפור. It sets the base rule that the next steps will analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children may bathe, anoint, and so on, but shoes are singled out as forbidden. The puzzle is why shoes are different from everything else.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Young children are permitted in all of them,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all five things forbidden on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: except for wearing a sandal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the wooden-leg discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are permitted in all יום כיפור restrictions except wearing shoes.

steps.title: Why are shoes different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes wearing shoes different from the other activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about wearing a sandal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why shoes are forbidden for children when everything else is allowed. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the other activities are allowed for children, there must be a special reason that shoes alone are forbidden. The גמרא wants that reason spelled out.

phrases.english: What is different about wearing a sandal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exception in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason shoes alone are forbidden for children.

steps.title: People will say adults put them on
steps.stepSummary: Shoes are forbidden because observers will say adults put them on the child on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people will say: adults did this for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a small child cannot put on shoes alone. People will assume an adult dressed him on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is about appearances. Onlookers would think an adult did a forbidden act for the child today.

phrases.english: Because they will say: adults did this for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shoes are forbidden because of what onlookers will think: that adults put them on the child today.

steps.title: The same worry applies to bathing and anointing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: people could also say adults bathed or anointed the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: With those other activities too, people will say: adults did this for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Bathing and anointing are also done to a child by adults, so the same worry should apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry about appearances forbids shoes, it should also forbid bathing and anointing. Yet the ברייתא allows those.

phrases.english: About those too they will say:
adults did this for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The appearance-based reason for forbidding shoes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same appearance concern would apply to bathing and anointing, which are permitted.

steps.title: Bathing could have been done yesterday
steps.stepSummary: With bathing and anointing, people will assume it was done the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: With bathing and anointing, one could say they did it for him yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a clean or oiled child does not prove anything was done today. It may have been done before יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathing and anointing leave no clear sign of when they happened. Onlookers would not conclude that a forbidden act was done today.

phrases.english: Bathing and anointing:
say that they did it for him yesterday.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְחִיצָה וְסִיכָה, אֵימַר מֵאֶתְמוֹל עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bathing and anointing raise the same appearance problem as shoes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Onlookers can assume bathing and anointing were done the day before.

steps.title: Shoes could also be from yesterday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: people could say the shoes were put on yesterday too.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a sandal too, say they put it on him yesterday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same answer to shoes. Maybe the child has been wearing them since the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'it was done yesterday' removes the worry for bathing, it should remove the worry for shoes as well. Then shoes would not be different.

phrases.english: A sandal too:
say that they did it for him yesterday!

steps.triggerLanguage: סַנְדָּל נָמֵי, אֵימַר מֵאֶתְמוֹל עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 15 against the shoe rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between shoes and bathing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'done yesterday' assumption could apply to shoes as well.

steps.title: Nobody sleeps in shoes
steps.stepSummary: Shoes cannot be from yesterday, since no one sleeps in shoes, as שמואל said.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a sandal it is impossible that they put it on yesterday. As שמואל said: whoever wants a taste of death should put on shoes and go to sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that shoes come off at night. If a child is wearing them in the morning, someone put them on today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's saying shows that sleeping in shoes is harmful, so no one does it. Shoes on a child therefore look like a fresh act done on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: With a sandal, it is impossible
that they did it for him yesterday.
As Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמִיטְעַם טַעְמָא דְמִיתוּתָא —
phrases.english: One who wants to taste the taste of death
should put on shoes and go to sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַנְדָּל לָא אֶפְשָׁר דְּמֵאֶתְמוֹל עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction supported by a statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shoes could have been put on the day before.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shoes are removed at night, so shoes worn today were put on today.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says children are permitted outright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא says children are permitted from the start, so appearance cannot be the issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches that they are permitted from the outset!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole approach. The ברייתא calls these activities fully permitted for children, so even doing them today is fine and nothing looks wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an adult may bathe a child even on יום כיפור, there is no improper act for onlookers to suspect. So the 'people will say' reason does not explain the shoe rule.

phrases.english: But it teaches that they are permitted from the outset!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the entire appearance-based line of steps 13-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'people will say adults did it' explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'permitted' means adults may do these acts today, so there is no suspicion to avoid.

steps.title: Things needed for growth were not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis forbade what a child does not need for growth and did not forbid what the child needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: things that are not needed for their growth, the Rabbis decreed against. Things that are needed for their growth, the Rabbis did not decree against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old reason and gives a new one. Bathing and anointing help a child grow, so they stay permitted, but shoes are not needed, so they are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule now depends on the child's actual needs, not on appearances. This fits the ברייתא's word 'permitted' fully.
steps.whatToRemember: Children may bathe and be anointed on יום כיפור because they need these to grow. Shoes are forbidden because a child does not need them.

phrases.english: Rather:
those that are not for their growth
the Rabbis decreed against them;
those that are for their growth
the Rabbis did not decree against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with a new principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shoe rule is about how things look to onlookers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule depends on whether the activity is needed for the child's growth.

steps.title: אביי's mother on what children need
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes his mother: children need hot water and oil, then egg with כותחא, then vessels to break, as רבה did for his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said: my mother told me: a baby's growth needs hot water and oil. When he grows a little, egg with כותחא. When he grows a little more, vessels to break. Like רבה, who bought cracked clay vessels for his children, and they broke them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the growth principle. It shows that hot water and oil, meaning bathing and anointing, are real needs for a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's mother lists bathing and anointing as basic needs for a baby. That proves they fall under 'needed for growth,' while shoes are not on the list. The רבה story shows that even breaking things is a real developmental need.

keyTerms.meaning: Egg with כותחא, a milk-based dip

steps.confusionAlert: 'אם' here means אביי's foster mother, the woman who raised him. אביי often quotes her advice.

phrases.english: As Abaye said: Mother told me:
The growth of a baby
needs hot water and oil.
When he grows a little: egg with kutacha.
When he grows a little more: breaking vessels.
Like Rabba,

phrases.aramaic: זָבֵין לְהוּ מָאנֵי גְּזִיזֵי דְּפַחְרָא לִבְנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: who bought cracked clay vessels for his children,
and they would break them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the principle of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That bathing and anointing are growth needs for a child.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי quoting his mother, and the practice of רבה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: king and bride wash their faces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a king and a bride may wash their faces.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king and the bride may wash their faces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes this line. It is setting up a question about who taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new ruling but a quote that opens a new discussion. The next step asks for its source.

phrases.english: The king and the bride
may wash their faces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king and a bride may wash their faces on יום כיפור.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught this ruling in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who is the author of this line in the משנה. It is setting up the identification that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know whose view this is, which suggests the ruling is not agreed by everyone. The answer will reveal a dispute.

phrases.english: Our mishna, whose is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the quoted ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תנא behind the ruling that a king and bride may wash their faces.

steps.title: It is רבי חנניא בן תרדיון quoting רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the תנא קמא forbids a king and bride to wash, and a new mother to wear shoes. רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, quoting רבי אליעזר, permits both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, as was taught: The king and the bride may not wash their faces. רבי חנניא בן תרדיון says in the name of רבי אליעזר: the king and the bride may wash their faces. A new mother may not wear a sandal. רבי חנניא בן תרדיון says in the name of רבי אליעזר: a new mother may wear a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי חנניא בן תרדיון. It brings a ברייתא where he, quoting רבי אליעזר, permits what the first opinion forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the permission for the king and the bride is a disputed view. It is the view of רבי חנניא בן תרדיון in the name of רבי אליעזר, and the משנה follows it. The same pair also argues about whether a new mother may wear shoes.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who just gave birth

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's permission for the king and the bride follows רבי חנניא בן תרדיון in the name of רבי אליעזר. He also permits a new mother to wear shoes, and the first opinion disagrees on both.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon,
as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַכִּלָּה לֹא יִרְחֲצוּ אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: The king and the bride may not wash their faces.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
The king and the bride may wash their faces.
A new mother may not wear a sandal.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
A new mother may wear a sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי חנניא בן תרדיון quoting רבי אליעזר, against the first opinion in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The reason a king may wash his face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's leniency. For a king, the reason is the פסוק: 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? A king may wash, because it is written: 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר lets a king and a bride wash their faces on יום כיפור. It starts with the king and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous step we learned only that רבי אליעזר permits washing. Now the גמרא supplies his reason. The פסוק teaches that a king must always appear beautiful and dignified before his people, so even on יום כיפור he may wash his face.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He's asking why רבי אליעזר is lenient here.

phrases.english: A king: because it is written:
"Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty."
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק from ישעיהו 33:17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's ruling quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי אליעזר permit a king to wash his face?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק teaches that a king should always be seen in his beauty.

steps.title: The reason a bride may wash her face
steps.stepSummary: A bride may wash her face so that she does not look unattractive to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for a bride? So that she should not become unattractive to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason for the second leniency. A bride may wash so that her new husband does not find her unattractive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the king, the bride's reason comes from logic, not from a פסוק. Early in a marriage the bond between husband and wife is still forming, so her appearance matters especially.

phrases.english: A bride, what is the reason?
So that she should not become unattractive to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to the king's reason; completes the explanation of רבי אליעזר's two leniencies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי אליעזר permit a bride to wash her face?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So that she does not become unattractive to her husband.

steps.title: רב asks how long a woman counts as a bride
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי חייא for how long after the wedding a woman is still considered a כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: Until when is she considered a bride?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks how long the special 'bride' status lasts. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency depends on her being a כלה, so we need to know where that status ends. Without a time limit, the rule would have no clear boundary.

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Chiya:
A bride, until how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא: כַּלָּה עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit of the bride status that was just used as the reason for leniency.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: For how long after her wedding is a woman considered a כלה?

steps.title: Thirty days, proven from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers from a ברייתא: we do not stop a bride from using jewelry or adornments for all of the first thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it was taught in a ברייתא: We do not withhold adornments from a bride for all thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers that a woman counts as a bride for thirty days, and he proves it from a ברייתא about adornments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that during the first thirty days, even when adornments are normally restricted (for example, during mourning), a bride's appearance is protected. The same thirty-day period therefore defines 'bride' for washing on יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
We do not withhold or prevent

steps.whatToRemember: A king may wash because of a פסוק, and a bride may wash so she stays attractive to her husband. 'Bride' means the first thirty days of marriage.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it was taught in a baraita:
We do not withhold adornments from the bride
for all thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, כִּדְתַנְיָא: אֵין מוֹנְעִין תַּכְשִׁיטִין מִן הַכַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question about the length of bride status.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thirty days, based on the ברייתא about not withholding adornments from a bride.

steps.title: A new mother may wear shoes because of the cold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a חיה (a woman who recently gave birth) may wear shoes: because of the cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: A new mother may wear shoes, because of the cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other leniency in the ברייתא and explains why a new mother may wear shoes on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After giving birth she is weak, and walking barefoot on a cold floor could make her sick. Her health concern overrides the ban on wearing shoes.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who recently gave birth
May put on the sandal (wear shoes)

phrases.english: A new mother may wear the sandal
because of the cold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 23 and explains its second leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new mother may wear shoes on יום כיפור because of the danger from cold.

steps.title: שמואל: shoes allowed when scorpions are a danger
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a person fears scorpions, he may wear shoes on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If it is because of the danger of a scorpion, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds another case where wearing shoes is allowed: when walking barefoot could expose someone to scorpions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This extends the idea from the new mother. Any real danger to health permits shoes, and this applies to anyone, not only a weak person.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
If it is because of the danger of a scorpion
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אִם מֵחֲמַת סַכָּנַת עַקְרָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further exception to the ban on shoes, based on danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing shoes on יום כיפור is permitted when there is a danger of scorpions.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the יום כיפור restrictions on comfort give way to real physical danger.

steps.title: New topic: eating a large date's volume, and רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, that one who eats the volume of a large date is liable. It then introduces a question from רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who eats the volume of a large date.' רב פפא asked:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה: the amount of food that makes someone liable on יום כיפור. It then sets up a question from רב פפא, which will appear in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step changes topic, from washing and shoes to the amount of eating that makes a person liable. The words בעי רב פפא only introduce his question; its content comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The volume of a large date (the amount that makes one liable)

phrases.english: One who eats the volume of a large date.
Rav Pappa asked:
phrases.notes: His actual question comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹכֵל כְּכוֹתֶבֶת הַגַּסָּה. בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of washing and shoes and begins a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who eats food the volume of a large date on יום כיפור is liable.
